questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to be in a mandarin speaking country since i already speak the language a bit. I also wanted to live in a big city, because there is just so much going on. Therefore i choose Taipei.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the destination was amazing, the only reason i did not give 10 marks is because i feel like the teaching at National Taiwan University (NTU) was not that good

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was okay. There is a website where you do the application. It's stated what kind of documents you need to upload. The only thing that was a bit difficult to find out was how to do the health report check in TW, but i figured it out. They sent a lot of emails, so it can be a bit confusing to remember everything, better write it down in your calendar. I was also assigned a local student buddy i could ask questions to. She sent me an email and then i could message her if i had any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a campus tour where the local students showed is around the campus. We also had some kind of "information day" where people from the international office gave us information about how stuff works at NTU.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was really easy. I personally found housing from a Facebook group. It's easy to find them, just type in something ala Taipei rental. Be aware of scams though.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware of what contract you sign. Mine contract said if someone else did not lease the room after me, i would lose one month of deposit. Luckily another person rented the room right after me, but be aware of what is signed. My landlord spoke fluent english, and the contract itself was in english so if it's in chinese you need to be more aware.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I applied for a dorm, but ended up with one where 4 person live in the same room and was far away from the city. Which is why i decided to find housing on my own. it was important for me to live in the city, so it was easy to join events. Compared to Copenhagen the rental price in Taipei is cheap, so i think it's worth it do live of campus unless you get a dorm on or close to campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Felt a bit unnecessary to be honest, i don't understand how i could not just be online

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You first upload the relevant documents online. Then there is a big registration date where every student gets assigned a time to show up. You need to bring documents with you, and then you go through some stations to get the documents checked. If everything is okay, you receive your student ID card.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office could be contacted if there was anything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I needed at least 12 credits. After applying for courses ended i only got 6 credits. I remember there are two rounds where you list the courses you want. After this the add/drop period starts. Student can drop courses, and then other people can add them. courses that are full might still have spaces for students if you go to the professor and ask for a code to join the courses. Therefore i went to two classes at their first lecture to ask the professor for a code. An email also works. On the course website, you will be able to see what to do in order to get the course, some might be completely full though.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: During course registration in the first two rounds the strategy is to apply for everything, and then drop the courses you don't want. The courses you do not get but want to have, go ask the professor for an add code. So don't get worried if you end up with too few courses in the two rounds, it all changes again in the add/drop period

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The courses i took were all open for graduate students. There was no exercise class which i felt was missing because you learn a lot in exercise classes. Generally speaking i did not rate the academic part that good at NTU, i did not learn much there. But i believe it's also my own mistake because i did not study as much as i do normally at UCPH.

Also be aware that the passing grade is different for undergrad and grad students! I only realized this one month into the semester, which made me very stressed. After the semester i realized that it seems like the professors are very large at grading at NTU, especially towards exchange students so i would not worry much about not passing courses. I myselves got okay grades without studying that much

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 2 of the courses i had was really difficult and i had a hard time keeping up. One of them i understood almost everything so no problem there. The last one the professor was really bad at teaching, so i did not go to class that much.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I had one class where the professor would cold call students to answer questions, that is rare in UCPH. Other that than it reminds of UCPH, a professor uses some slides to go through the lecture. As i had mentioned before i had no exercise classes.
The grading depends on the class. It can be a mix of quizzes, presentations, attendance, final exam, midterm and etc. For my classes i was a mix between presentations, assignment and maybe a final exam. For example presentation could be 25%, final exam 50% and assignments 25%. This kind of grading system causes the workload to be higher, because you need to make sure your assignments are good. At UCPH we normally our final grade is just the final exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Computational methods in econometrics: Very difficult course, would not recommend because you need to spend a lot of time on it. Also you only learn the theory, but the assignments are about coding. So you essentially need to learn the coding yourself.

Market & strategy. Can recommend. The professor cold calls, but his teaching is really good. I learned a lot from this course. The "final exam" is a research proposal which was actually quite fun to make.

Advanced applied econometrics and international trade: Can not recommend. The professor is really bad at teaching. Also the professor is not good at giving information out and changes plans a lot. The final exam felt more like a memory test rather than an exam.

Spatial economics: Mixed feelings. The course is really interesting but also very difficult. So it depends on how much you want to spent on studying while on exchange. If you're willing to spend time studying i would say go for it.

I also had chinese for fun, i can recommend it. I was placed in intermediate 1A after the placement test. The teacher was really good and it's also a good way to make new friends :D

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did this above

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Comments to above: I walked to school so did not spend money on that, tbh i have no idea how much i spent riding public transport each month. 

Also the phone plan i do not remember. You can get a deal at Chunghwa telecom in the airport where you buy get a student discount with unlimited data. You pay for everything at once.

Internet was included in my rent. 

Personal spending i also just typed something in.

Unexpected costs: I did much more travel than i expected to do. But it's worth it, Taiwan is so beautiful so make sure to travel around and see stuff!!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Actually the food was a bit more expensive than i expected. Travelling was really cheap. The cheapest way to get around is probably by bus. Hostels in Taiwan are super good quality. All of the hostels i stayed at provided soap, and a lot of them provide slippers.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: NTU campus is amazing. There's a lot of clubs you can join, and there are sport facilities such as baseball. football, swimming, tennis, volleyball and probably more if you are into that.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There's a list of clubs. If you find anything interested go for it. Would be a good way also to meet local students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel around Taiwan. As said before it's cheap and there is so much stuff to see in Taiwan. It's really ideal to travel Taiwan because it's so small and public transport is good. 

I personally enjoyed hiking. Coming from Denmark which is a flat country, hiking mountains was really fun. If you plan ahead there are some mountains that requires permits. So if you wanna climb for example Jade mountain plan ahead and apply for the permit.

There's also a lot of stuff to do in Taipei, i visited parks, historical landmarks, went to museums, went hiking. National palace museum is a must visit!

I would recommend getting a international driver's licence before going, it will make it easier to get a scooter which is essential when going to the small islands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have chinese background, i also lived in Beijing for 6 months in my gap year and have been a lot of times to China to visit my family. Since Taiwanese culture and Chinese culture have some overlap, it was easier for me to adapt. For me therefore it was not that difficult, but hearing from my international friends it seems like it was not that difficult to adapt.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Language exchange is a good opportunity to meet locals, surprisingly i found someone who wanted to learn Danish. Go join a club on campus, use apps.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
When ordering food, seems like you just walk up and talk without the worker asking you first. Normally in Denmark i always wait for the worker to say Hi or something, otherwise it feels rude. But other than that i did not experience any problems, and this is a minor one because when ordering at restaurants, you normally just get a paper menu and cross of what you want to eat.

Otherwise not really much problems, but as said before i had been to China a lot of times.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are really friendly in Taiwan. Also Taiwan is very safe

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get ready for the bureaucracy, a lot of stuff needs to be done before you go, and also when you arrive in Taiwan. 

In Taiwan cash is still king. So you need to bring cash with you. It would be a good idea to do research into which banks offer the cheapest ATM fee.  I personally only used Bank of Taiwan. Some places take linepay where you can connect your debit/credit card. Here i used revolut so there would be no exchange fee when paying in the weekdays.

Travel and enjoy the experience. You will miss Taiwan a lot when getting home, remember that school is not everything. It's in my opinion just as important to travel and meet new people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There's a taiwanese like reddit called PTT. Here you can read Taiwanese students write reports about courses they took. It's of course in Chinese but google translate is fine. You prob have to do the search in chinese also. For example to look up report for market and strategy i could type "ptt 市場與策略" which is market and strategy in chinese. It probably also works if you type in the course number. The first result is this :
https://www.ptt.cc/bbs/NTUcourse/M.1498144948.A.B8F.html
Where a local student writes about market and strategy. I believe the course list shows both the chinese name and english name.
Another website which can be used to see evaluations about courses is
https://rating.myntu.me/
. I personally never used the website, but i saw someone post about it in the NTU facebook group.
I think there was a lack of english courses at NTU, if you do economics there's a better layout of the course list at the economics department website.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The friendship you made when on exchange. You make friends with people all over the world! 

Being able to practise my mandarin was also nice. 

Travelling around Taiwan with friends and also alone was amazing. There's a lot of different food to try also.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Definitely the language. My chinese is probably like kindergarten level so i would have difficulty talking and understanding. A lot of menus are in Chinese only, so you would have to use your phone to translate the stuff. 

It was also difficult balancing school and travelling. The workload is higher at NTU than at UCPH. You're still a student so you still need to study, but at the same time you of course want to experience stuff. I personally felt like i had to turn down too many stuff in order to get my assignments done. The final month was also very stressful, with a mix of presentations, paper reports, final exam.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
It can get really hot in Taiwan in the summer. I was travelling in end of june, and i had to go into 7-11 to get some AC from time to time.

The scallion pancake (蔥抓餅) close to campus gongguan（公館) is super good, it's on the michelin bib gourmand list. 

Enjoy it!!! I miss it a lot

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
